tool_input.command: find src/test/java -iname '*Lexer*'; find src/test/java -iname '*ExtendedBufferedReaderTest*' -exec cat {} \; | head -80

result:
Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java` with 32 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `Lexer`'s tokenizing (simple/quoted/escaped tokens, delimiters, multi-char delimiters, comments, EOL variants CR/LF/CRLF), boundary cases (empty input, trailing delimiter/content at EOF, no final newline), error cases (unterminated quoted token, invalid char after encapsulated token, escape at EOF), format options (`ignoreEmptyLines`, `ignoreSurroundingSpaces`, `lenientEof`, `trailingData`), and the smaller helper methods (`isEndOfFile`, `isStartOfLine`, `isQuoteChar`, `isCommentStart`, `isEscape`, `readEscape`, `trimTrailingSpaces`, `close`/`isClosed`, `getCurrentLineNumber`, `getFirstEol`, `getBytesRead`).

All 32 tests pass against `./_tools/test.sh`. Two of my initial expectations were wrong rather than real bugs (I corrected them after investigation):
- A trailing delimiter at EOF (e.g. `"a,"`) legitimately produces a `Token.Type.EOF` with `isReady=true` and empty content — `CSVParser.nextRecord()` explicitly treats that as the record's final empty field, so it's by design, not a bug.
- An escape character at end-of-stream (e.g. `"a\\"`) is documented in `Lexer.readEscape()`'s javadoc as throwing `CSVException`, so that's expected, not a bug.

No genuine bugs were found in `Lexer` during this testing — all behavior matched the documented/intended design once my test expectations were corrected.
